- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) or negative, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to compensate for bearish sentiment bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overreacts and overshoots; cap forecast increase to 5% max from prior peak to avoid overcorrection.
- If recent history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model tends to ignore trend; apply slight upward bias to counteract downward momentum.
- When sentiment is neutral or positive (≥0.7) and price is trending upward, model often underestimates upside; add 2–5% buffer to forecast to capture sentiment-driven momentum.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period volatility; increase forecast by 1–3% for days 25–30 if sentiment is positive or neutral.
- If sentiment history shows sudden shift from negative to positive (e.g., -0.14 → 0.82), model lags in adjusting; apply early correction by 1–2% to first 3–5 days of forecast.
